title: The Sophistry Measure: the Sophistical Refutations Read as an Instrument for Machine-Composed Knowledge (EA-SOPHISTRY-01 v1.0)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The sophistry measure reads Aristotle's Sophistical Refutations from the seated Greek as an instrument for machine-composed knowledge. Sophistry, by SE 1, is wisdom that appears and is not, and the sophist makes money from the appearance; the measure records, at an address, the gap between what a composition presents itself as carrying and what it carries, finding by finding, each a transformation reconstructed from the texts with its witness, countertest and repair, and no scalar. Its governing condition is the composition's claim to adequacy. Its case is the asynthetic ChatGPT observation of 2026-11-01, PER 0.042 with eleven of twelve atoms present, where the measurement target itself had promoted a received, unendorsed plate of Notebook X (X-012) to the archive's definition and substituted that locus for a concept developed across eight deposits; the case is exhibited at six loci. A second reading of the book gives eleven loci, each marked direct instance, structural extension or interpretive connection: the counters (σύμβολα moved like ψῆφοι, finite names for unlimited things), distance, the genus divided by function and incentive (χρηματιστική ἀπὸ σοφίας φαινομένης), no division by the thought, five aims as effect types, accent and the editor's διόρθωσις, the this and the such (X24 and the third man), the veiled man, sharpness, the solution addressed to the questioner, and the ending measured in The Particle. The measure's interfaces with the Capture Registry, the developmental dossier, PER, the Negative of the Negative and SPXI-gnΩsis are specified, and its locus is set where computation and philology meet: a witness is a philological object, a check a computational one.
content_type: Specification (measurement instrument, with a philological reading)
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed by Claude (Anthropic) in session on 2026-11-01 under Lee Sharks's direction: the second reading of the Sophistical Refutations from the Greek seated in the archive, every locus checked at its line; the orientation, joins and requirements; v0.2 transformed in place on three outside reviews (DeepSeek, Gemini, ChatGPT), each claim checked against the archive before adoption. The pilot dossier the specification builds on (taxonomy, case units, prototype) was produced in a separate ChatGPT session at Lee Sharks's direction and is not deposited here. The idea of the measure, the X24 correction and the decision to deposit are Lee Sharks's.
methodology: The Sophistical Refutations read in the Greek seated at data/corpora/aristotle/text/tlg040-De_sophisticis_elenchis.txt, every quoted locus given by line in that file and checked there. The asynthetic case exhibited from the seated texts (#524, #1550), the target's intake part and the registry observation, each span checked at its locus; the registry's per_dim read atom by atom. Three outside reviews checked claim by claim against the archive before adoption; corrections recorded in the commit history. The pilot dossier's counts (48 types, 27 case units, 12 tests) are reported as the dossier states them; its bundle is not yet in the archive.
falsification_conditions: The measure fails as an instrument if two readers running the full finding record (§3.2) on the same case cannot agree on its witness and reconstruction; if a finding's countertest cannot be stated; if its types cannot be keyed to SR's loci with an explicit relation (direct instance, structural extension, interpretive connection); or if a repair passes the original test without addressing the dependency. A Greek join fails if the seated text at the cited line does not say what the section quotes.

wiki_article: The Sophistry Measure (EA-SOPHISTRY-01, version 1.0) is a specification by Lee Sharks, deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 1 November 2026, that reads Aristotle's Sophistical Refutations from the seated Greek as an instrument for machine-composed knowledge. Taking Aristotle's definition of sophistry as wisdom that appears and is not, it records, at a Capture Registry address, the gap between what a composition presents itself as carrying and what it carries. Each finding is a transformation reconstructed from the texts, with an exact witness, a reconstruction, a type keyed to the book's chapters, its strongest alternative reading, a countertest and the smallest repair; the measure gives no scalar. Its governing condition is the composition's claim to adequacy: what was asked, what scope the answer announces, and which omitted relation changes the answer at that scope. Its case is an asynthetic-synthesis observation scored at a Provenance Erasure Rate of 0.042 whose measurement target had itself promoted a received, unendorsed plate of Notebook X to the archive's definition, which the paper exhibits at six loci. A second reading of the book supplies eleven loci, among them the counters (names as σύμβολα moved like ψῆφοι), the division of the genus by what it secures, the five aims of disputation, accent and the editor's διόρθωσις, the this and the such, and the veiled man, each marked as a direct instance, a structural extension or an interpretive connection. The paper sets out the measure's interfaces with the Capture Registry, PER, the Negative of the Negative and SPXI-gnΩsis, and places it where computation and philology meet.

X24 in EA-SOPHISTRY-01: one location of an entity developed across several sources presented, unmarked, as the developed entity, where the composition claims more than its selected locus warrants; accurate quotation of the locus does not discharge it.

In EA-SOPHISTRY-01, the record of an entity's dated source locations, what each adds, applies, revises or leaves open, the relations among them, and the voice and endorsement of each proposition; linked to the entity's /non composition and kept apart from it so the composition stays auditable.

In EA-SOPHISTRY-01, the condition a finding records before any operation is typed: what was asked, what scope the answer announces, and which omitted relation materially changes the answer at that scope.

In EA-SOPHISTRY-01, after SE 22, the status a composition gives a quotation it sets out: setting a locus out (ekthesis) is no fault, and the finding lies in conceding it the standing of the developed entity.
